title: Chouhan Assures Punjab Farmers India Won't Sign Trade Deal Harming Agriculture
excerpt: At a BJP rally during Punjab's Rakhar Punia fair, the agriculture minister said no trade agreement would be signed that harms Indian farmers, while positioning the party for the 2027 state elections.
body:
• Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan assured Punjab farmers that India would not sign any trade agreement with the US that harms their interests
  • Chouhan said no final trade agreement with the US exists at present, and any future deal would ensure farmer protections
  • The BJP rally at Baba Bakala Sahib during the Rakhar Punia fair signals the party's push for independent standing ahead of 2027 Punjab elections
  • Chouhan attacked the AAP government on agricultural policy, law and order, and alleged misuse of central funds

Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan used a major Sikh religious gathering in Punjab on Friday to reassure the state's farming community that India would not sign any trade agreement with the United States or any other country if it harmed Indian farmers.

Addressing a BJP political conference organized during the Rakhar Punia fair at Baba Bakala Sahib, Chouhan said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made it clear that farmer interests would remain paramount in any trade negotiations, NDTV reported.

No Final Deal With US

Chouhan stressed that no final trade agreement with the US exists at present. "If an agreement is reached in the future, the Centre would ensure that the interests of farmers remained protected," he said.

The issue carries particular weight in Punjab, where agriculture is both an economic backbone and a political flashpoint. With the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections on the horizon, the BJP is working to strengthen its connections with the farming community, making Chouhan's assurance on the trade deal a centerpiece of the party's messaging.

India's trade relationship with the United States has become a defining issue in domestic politics. The Modi government has faced criticism from the opposition Congress party over the terms of a proposed trade agreement, with Congress alleging the deal could undermine Indian agriculture. Chouhan has repeatedly defended the government's position, arguing that key agricultural products — including wheat, rice, soybean, dairy, and spices — have been kept out of any trade concessions.

Sharp Attack on AAP Government

Chouhan turned his speech into a pointed critique of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's AAP government, questioning what it had done for Punjab's farmers. He said he had written to Mann seeking implementation of a crop insurance scheme but alleged the scheme remained unimplemented.

"You have tried everyone, now give BJP a chance."

— Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Agriculture Minister

The agriculture minister also accused the AAP government of misusing funds released by the Centre for various schemes, particularly targeting it over MGNREGA allocations. He described the party's governance failures as having surpassed those of the Congress.

Chouhan attacked the state government on law and order, women's safety, and gangsterism. Referring to the Raksha Bandhan occasion, he questioned whether women in Punjab felt safe amid incidents of crime and alleged that gangsterism had become a serious challenge in the state.

He also defended the Centre's broader agricultural policies, saying farmers were being provided fertilizers at subsidized rates and accusing the state government of failing to adequately address agricultural concerns in Punjab.

BJP's Independent Punjab Strategy

The BJP organized its own political stage at the Rakhar Punia gathering, a move observers see as evidence of the party's intent to contest Punjab independently rather than relying on its traditional alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal.

On the possibility of an alliance with the Akali Dal, Chouhan said the party's leadership had indicated that "all possibilities would be considered" but declined to elaborate further.

Chouhan outlined the BJP's vision for Punjab's agricultural future, emphasizing crop diversification, greater agricultural processing, and increased exports. He also highlighted the Centre's Lakhpati Didi initiative, claiming approximately three crore women had already benefited and that the target was to reach six crore.

Chouhan described the gathering as more than a show of political strength, portraying it as a declaration of the BJP's commitment to Punjab's development and its ambition to form the next government in the state. He ended his address by offering prayers for Indians reported missing amid floods in Nepal.
